title: Why Linux is making a desktop comeback

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: Why is Linux, once a niche server OS, now gaining traction on the desktop? What’s driving this shift?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Modern distros like Fedora and Pop!_OS offer polished UIs, Wayland for security, and snaps for universal app packaging.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: But adoption faces barriers—lack of mainstream apps, user unfamiliarity, and corporate inertia that favors Windows and macOS.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Developers are creating better drivers, improving hardware support, and platforms like Flatpak are expanding software availability.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A future where Linux becomes the default desktop OS could democratize computing and reduce vendor lock-in.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: Linux’s resurgence signals a shift toward open, customizable, and inclusive desktop ecosystems.

video_cue: A split-screen showing a Linux desktop running creative tools alongside a Windows and macOS interface.
